'''Dillon Brooks''' (born January 22, 1996) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player who most recently played for the [[University of Oregon]]. He is also a member of the [[Canadian men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]].

==College career==
Brooks, a 6'7" [[small forward]] from [[Mississauga]], [[Ontario]], came to Oregon after playing at [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]]. As a freshman, he averaged 11.5 points per game and was named to the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12 Conference]] all-freshman team.<ref name=yahoo/> As a sophomore, Brooks led the Ducks to the [[Pac-12 Conference]] regular season title and a top ten national ranking. At the close of the season, he was named first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]]<ref>{{cite web | last = Alger| first = Tyson| title = Dillon Brooks and Elgin Cook earn 1st-team all-Pac-12 honors | work = [[OregonLive.com]] | date = March 7, 2016 | url = http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2016/03/dillon_brooks_and_elgin_cook_e.html | accessdate = March 12, 2016}}</ref> and a third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] by the [[Sporting News]]. He was also named the District IX player of the year by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] (USBWA).<ref>{{cite web | last = Alger| first = Tyson| title = Dana Altman and Dillon Brooks win U.S. Basketball Writers Association awards | work = [[OregonLive.com]] | date = March 8, 2016 | url = http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2016/03/dana_altman_and_dillon_brooks.html | accessdate = March 12, 2016}}</ref> Brooks averaged 16.7 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game.<ref name="healthy">{{cite news|last1=Medcalf|first1=Myron|title=With a healthy Dillon Brooks, Oregon can crash party and win it all|url=http://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/post/_/id/116130/with-a-healthy-brooks-oregon-can-crash-the-party-and-win-it-all|accessdate=October 11, 2016|work=[[ESPN]]|date=October 4, 2016}}</ref>

After the conclusion of the 2015–16 season, Brooks said he would remain with Oregon for a third season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://oregon.247sports.com/Bolt/Dillon-Brooks-Addresses-NBA-Decision--44496207|title=Dillon Brooks Addresses NBA Decision|author=Prehm, Matt|publisher=247 Sports|date=March 26, 2016|accessdate=March 27, 2016}}</ref> He suffered a foot injury in the summer of 2016 and did not play in Oregon's offseason trip to Spain.<ref name="healthy"/> On November 7, 2016, Brooks was named to the [[Associated Press]]' preseason All-America team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/duke-s-allen-leads-ap-preseason-all-america-team-110216 |title=Duke's Allen leads AP preseason All-America team |publisher=[[Foxsports.com]] |date=November 2, 2016 |accessdate=November 12, 2016}}</ref>

Shortly after the [[2016–17 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|2016–17 season]], he declared himself eligible for the [[2017 NBA draft]] and hired an [[Sports agent|agent]], ending his college career.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/ducks/index.ssf/2017/04/dillon_brooks_oregon_career_is.html |title=Dillon Brooks' Oregon career is over as he declares for NBA draft, hires agent |first=Andrew |last=Greif |newspaper=[[The Oregonian]] |date=April 12, 2017 |accessdate=May 1, 2017}}</ref>

==International career==
Brooks represented Canada in the [[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games|2015 Pan American Games]], where the team won the silver medal.<ref name=yahoo>{{cite web | last = Denomme| first = Ian| title = Canada settles for silver in basketball at Pan Am Games, but future looks bright | work = [[Yahoo.com]] | date = July 25, 2016 | url = https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/blogs/eh-game/canada-settles-for-silver-in-basketball-at-pan-am-games--but-future-looks-bright-000909709.html | accessdate = March 12, 2016}}</ref>
